lines.trans: Guys, we have a disaster, our Max just crashed!
What do you mean crashed? He was flying on a plane!
He got a message that Vika is giving birth right now.
And he immediately jumped down with a parachute!
He got badly tangled in the lines and landed poorly.
Doctors just called me from his phone.
The doctors said that his condition is very serious.
Fedya, what have you and I done today?
We just wanted to play a harmless joke on him!

examples.text: Что вы наделали, Виктория?
examples.trans: What have you done, Victoria?

examples.text: Что, я зря пришла? Я надела костюм зайки!
examples.trans: What, did I come for nothing? I put on a bunny costume!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Оно просто никак не снимается, совсем застряло!
examples.trans: It just will not come off at all, it is completely stuck!

examples.text: Наверное, просто не могу забыть свою первую любовь.
examples.trans: I probably just cannot forget my first love.

examples.text: Понятно, тогда тебе просто надо немного развеяться!
examples.trans: I see, then you simply need to clear your head a bit!

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'обидно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы же просто безобидно пошутить над ним хотели!
examples.trans: We just wanted to play a harmless joke on him!

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно безобидно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite harmlessly and calmly.

пошутить.gloss: to joke, to make a joke

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шутить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to joke, to make a joke', paired with 'шутить'.

examples.text: Мы же просто безобидно пошутить над ним хотели!
examples.trans: We just wanted to play a harmless joke on him!

examples.text: Слушай, ты думаешь, не слишком жёстко мы пошутили?
examples.trans: Listen, do you think we did not joke too harshly?

examples.text: Мы просто пошутили, с Максом всё хорошо!
examples.trans: We were just joking, everything is fine with Max!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это уже девятнадцатый букет за одну неделю!
examples.trans: This is already the nineteenth bouquet in a single week!

examples.text: Понятно, тогда тебе просто надо немного развеяться!
examples.trans: I see, then you simply need to clear your head a bit!

examples.text: Тебе надо немного развеяться.
examples.trans: You need to clear your head a little.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Мы же просто безобидно пошутить над ним хотели!
examples.trans: We just wanted to play a harmless joke on him!

examples.text: Я хочу кофе.
examples.trans: I want coffee.

examples.text: Не хочешь, как хочешь.
examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello (on the phone)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Алло, Даша, твоё предложение насчёт Сочи ещё в силе?
examples.trans: Hello, Dasha, is your offer about Sochi still open?

examples.text: Алло, Макс, ты бы видел сейчас их бледные лица!
examples.trans: Hello, Max, you should have seen their pale faces just now!

examples.text: Алло? Кто это?
examples.trans: Hello? Who's this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, конечно помню, было такое дело.
examples.trans: Yes, of course I remember, that did happen.

examples.text: У тебя бывало, когда не знаешь, кто ухаживает?
examples.trans: Have you ever not known who was courting you?

examples.text: Бывало, я за него даже замуж вышла!
examples.trans: It has, I even married him!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Привет, Даша, как же я рад тебя видеть!
examples.trans: Hi, Dasha, how glad I am to see you!

examples.text: Нет, мы сами утром видели эту наглую машину.
examples.trans: No, we saw that insolent car ourselves this morning.

examples.text: Алло, Макс, ты бы видел сейчас их бледные лица!
examples.trans: Hello, Max, you should have seen their pale faces just now!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'their', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, они действительно сегодня очень свежие и красивые.
examples.trans: Yes, they really are very fresh and beautiful today.

examples.text: Ах, для такого дела? Тогда, конечно, они есть!
examples.trans: Oh, for a cause like that? Then of course I have some!

examples.text: Макс, ты с ума сошёл? Позвони ещё раз!
examples.trans: Max, have you lost your mind? Call them one more time!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pale, pallid').

examples.text: Алло, Макс, ты бы видел сейчас их бледные лица!
examples.trans: Hello, Max, you should have seen their pale faces just now!

examples.text: У него сегодня очень бледное лицо.
examples.trans: He has a very pale face today.

examples.text: Лицо бледное, руки немного дрожат.
examples.trans: Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'face; person' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Витя, раньше я пять лет мёрз на улице.
examples.trans: Vitya, in the past I froze on the street for five years.

examples.text: Алло, Макс, ты бы видел сейчас их бледные лица!
examples.trans: Hello, Max, you should have seen their pale faces just now!

examples.text: Очень тебе к лицу!
examples.trans: It really suits you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, ты думаешь, не слишком жёстко мы пошутили?
examples.trans: Listen, do you think we did not joke too harshly?

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson.

examples.text: Да, слушаю.
examples.trans: Yes, I'm listening.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'think, suppose', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Никогда бы не подумала, что ты разбираешься в цветах!
examples.trans: I never would have thought that you know so much about flowers!

examples.text: Кто бы мог подумать, что буду управлять отелем?
examples.trans: Who would have thought that I would manage a hotel?

examples.text: Не думала, что ты способен так красиво ухаживать.
examples.trans: I did not think that you were capable of courting so beautifully.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ум за папины деньги точно не купишь!
examples.trans: You certainly cannot buy brains with daddy's money!

examples.text: Пусть даже от какого-нибудь таинственного незнакомца.
examples.trans: Even if they come from some mysterious stranger.

examples.text: Да, конечно помню, было такое дело.
examples.trans: Yes, of course I remember, that did happen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Слушай, ты думаешь, не слишком жёстко мы пошутили?
examples.trans: Listen, do you think we did not joke too harshly?

examples.text: Скорую помощь ждать здесь будет слишком долго.
examples.trans: Waiting for an ambulance here will take too long.

examples.text: Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: Too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Слушай, ты думаешь, не слишком жёстко мы пошутили?
examples.trans: Listen, do you think we did not joke too harshly?

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно жёстко и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite harshly and calmly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это была моя бывшая одноклассница, у нас ничего не было!
examples.trans: That was my former classmate, nothing happened between us!

examples.text: Витя, ну как там поживает мой праздничный ужин?
examples.trans: Vitya, how is my festive dinner coming along?

examples.text: Не скромничай, такое упорство и такое редкое терпение!
examples.trans: Do not be modest, such persistence and such rare patience!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за него я должен лишние двадцать метров идти пешком!
examples.trans: Because of him I have to walk an extra twenty meters on foot!

examples.text: Ничего, я из-за них сам чуть с парашютом не прыгнул!
examples.trans: It is fine, because of them I almost jumped with a parachute myself!

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Только потом узнала, кто он на самом деле.
examples.trans: Only later did I find out who he really was.

examples.text: Нет, мы сами утром видели эту наглую машину.
examples.trans: No, we saw that insolent car ourselves this morning.

examples.text: Держи, вот самые лучшие и отборные тухлые яйца!
examples.trans: Here you go, the very best choice rotten eggs!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'almost, nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я эффектно появлюсь за столиком чуть позже!
examples.trans: And I will make a grand appearance at the table a bit later!

examples.text: Ничего, я из-за них сам чуть с парашютом не прыгнул!
examples.trans: It is fine, because of them I almost jumped with a parachute myself!

examples.text: Я чуть с парашютом не прыгнул!
examples.trans: I almost jumped with a parachute!
